passage: After failing two courses, Reena asked herself why, and then asked why again. She traced it back to the classes she missed when her mother was ill and to the way she hesitated to ask anyone for help. It had never been a matter of ability. Vijay took his marksheet to the academic advisor and explained what had happened. He learned when the backlog exams were, how the credit rules worked, and that a lighter load was possible next term. Yamini said nothing to anyone. She dreaded her family's reaction and skipped the forms for backlog exams. The deadlines passed, and her situation grew worse than the failure itself. Nishant checked his attendance and test scores every Sunday against his targets. When one subject kept scoring poorly for three weeks running, he stopped studying it alone and joined a group of classmates who met in the library.

qa.q: What did Vijay bring to the academic advisor?
How does Yamini's handling of her result differ from Vijay's, and what followed for each?
qa.a: Yamini said nothing and skipped the backlog forms, so deadlines lapsed and things got worse. Vijay explained openly to the advisor and learned about exam dates, credit rules and a lighter load.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when she skipped the backlog forms?
qa.a: She was afraid of how her family would react, so she avoided the problem.

qa.q: What could Yamini do now to make things better?
qa.a: She could speak to the advisor as soon as possible, ask what options remain, and tell a trusted family member or friend to have support. Facing it early keeps more choices open.

grounding: Students recover from a failed semester by tracing the cause, seeing an advisor, hiding the result, and tracking progress weekly.
